title: Introduce audit linker with context-aware KMS scopes and RBAC guard
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an audit-linker service that retrospectively enriches historical audit events with KMS scope and tenant-region context; adds RBAC admission guard to prevent cross-region KMS usage; migration script generates a compliance report for regulators.
description:
Context: Customers and auditors have asked for a way to link historical audit events to the KMS key scope and region used at the time of encryption. In some cases older audit envelopes lack the explicit KMS-region field that our current policies require. This PR implements a best-effort retrospective enrichment pipeline (audit-linker) and an RBAC admission guard that enforces context-aware KMS scoping for new requests.

What this PR does: - Adds services/audit/audit-linker: a service that scans historical audit envelopes, resolves KMS usage by consulting the KMS-usage index and service metadata, and writes a minimal enrichment record back to the audit store (audit.enrichments). The linker is idempotent and rate-limited. - Introduces pkg/security/kms_scope_resolver: resolves probable KMS region/tenant binding for legacy envelopes using heuristics (encryption-context, service tags, request timestamps). Heuristics are documented and conservative (prefer unknown rather than wrong). - Adds pkg/rbac/admission/kms_scope_guard: an admission controller plugin that rejects new operations which attempt to use a KMS key outside the allowed region for the requesting tenant or service role (RBAC v2 mapping). - Adds a migration script scripts/migrations/20250210-audit-linker-report that generates a compliance CSV listing enriched events and confidence scores for auditors. - E2E tests and unit tests added under tests/with fixtures for edge cases (missing encryption-context, stale service-tags). - Docs and runbook: docs/compliance/audit-linker.md and docs/runbooks/incident-audit-linker.md describing operation, throttles, and rollback.

Why this approach: We evaluated two options: (1) retroactive re-encryption or modification of historical audit envelopes (not acceptable for immutability guarantees), (2) store separate enrichment records that reference original events (chosen). The enrichment approach preserves immutability while meeting auditor requirements. The RBAC admission guard closes the gap for future requests so enrichment becomes progressively unnecessary.

Migration & rollout plan: - Stage 1 (canary): run audit-linker in read-only mode in canary region for 48h to measure enrichment rate and false-positive heuristics. - Stage 2 (opt-in): enable enrichment writes for dedicated customers who consent; collect compliance CSVs for review. - Stage 3 (enforce): enable RBAC admission guard cluster-wide and document policy. Backout: admission guard can be toggled via feature flag security.kms_scope_guard.enabled.

Testing: - Unit tests cover heuristic branches and failure modes. - Integration tests run audit-linker against a 10k-sample fixture (tests/fixtures/audit-sample-10k.json) to validate throughput and idempotence. - CI initially hit a flake on the index-resolver (fixed in commit 3).

Notes: - This PR is intentionally conservative about heuristic enrichment confidence. Enrichments include a confidence tag (high|medium|low|unknown) and do not change original envelopes. - We added audit.enrichments TTL of 90 days configurable per tenancy. - Performance: linker uses batched lookups and backpressure to avoid overloading the indexer.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration test fixture - [x] Docs - [x] Migration script - [x] Feature flag for admission guard - [x] Security review

Related: Linear ENG-4821, SEC-127, Support ticket SUP-3342.
